what: Boston Scientific makes devices used in less-invasive medicine: heart stents and catheters, pulsed field ablation systems for irregular heartbeat, endoscopy tools, urology devices and neuromodulation implants.
customers: Hospitals, cardiologists, electrophysiologists and surgical centres worldwide.
money: interventional cardiology, electrophysiology and structural heart devices
moat: Physicians trained on specific devices and techniques, plus clinical trial data that supports reimbursement and makes substitution risky.
risks: Growth has drawn competition into pulsed field ablation, its fastest-growing product
Hospitals negotiate hard on device prices
Acquisitions have raised debt to about $12 billion
Recalls or trial setbacks in implanted devices carry long liabilities
opportunities: Revenue grew about 20% in the last financial year, the fastest among large device makers
Pulsed field ablation is replacing older heart ablation methods quickly
An ageing population raises procedure volumes across its categories
watch: Organic revenue growth in electrophysiology and whether new entrants slow it.
